01Black Men Build · Special project of Working Families Organization, 2020 to 2024

Donor Communications & Funder Materials

Built with
EveryActionWordPressFigma

The challenge.

Supporters cared deeply but heard from us in bursts. Donors needed a steady reason to stay engaged and proof that their contributions were implemented.

What I drove.

  • A year-round giving rhythm: annual giving campaigns and monthly sustainer emails, so supporters heard from us consistently, not in bursts.
  • Audiences segmented by behavior for specialized communications. I used EveryAction activist codes to separate event attendees, volunteers, lapsed sustainers, and general supporters in our CRM. This shaped the language, calls to action, and cadence, reengaging them based on their interest and interaction with us and eliminating fatigue.
  • A Giving Tuesday sustainer push that asked one-time donors to become monthly sustainers, with a funding transparency section showing exactly where gifts go.
  • Regional lists created within our CRM to specialize communications across major swing states during active election cycles.
  • The 2023 Impact Report for high-dollar and small-dollar donors, with embedded donation forms and strategic links that made giving one step from the story.

The result.

Open rates rose 900%. The most engaged segment opened at 33.33%, nearly 7x our general list, and partnerships with Black Voters Matter and Black Futures Lab unlocked $250K in new revenue.

02Endeavor · Global nonprofit, 42 offices

AI Adoption: Change Without Losing Trust

Built with
ClaudeSlack AINotionPeople-Platform Comms Model

The challenge.

AI tools were arriving faster than guidance. Staff were wary, and leadership needed to protect a network built on trust and decades of institutional knowledge.

What I drove.

I built the AI governance communications that turned policy into plain guidance, then built the adoption engine around shared channels: a newsletter, a video series, learning sessions, and a platform champion in every office.

I developed and scaled the People-Platform Comms Model, which I first built for our cybersecurity rollout, into a standing partnership between the People and Platforms teams for ongoing change management.

I built advocacy into the model by selecting Platform Champions from each office to support launches and serve as strategic partners for our team and Managing Directors.

The result.

78% weekly active adoption of approved AI tools across 42 offices.

03Endeavor · Global nonprofit, 42 offices

Slack Architecture to Streamline Community

Built with
SlackSalesforceUser Research

The challenge.

Seventy-three channels, more than half inactive, duplicated, or unowned. People stopped trusting the shared space, so regions moved their conversations to WhatsApp, which posed a security risk for the organization. Staff had lost trust in Slack and wanted a space they could govern themselves.

What I drove.

I ran working sessions and interviews across regions, then a four-week parallel test of old and new channels, so data set the final structure instead of opinion or hypothesis. Every channel that survived got a one-sentence purpose, a named owner, consistent naming, and membership provisioning driven by Salesforce.

The result.

18 streamlined channels, with upwards of a 70% increase in channel communication in a 30-day period. 600 global staff engaged in a central community.

06Black Men Build · Editorial

A Publication That Meets People Where They Are

Built with
Print partnersDistribution modelingPublication audit

The challenge.

The organization's ideas lived online, and the people it most wanted to reach weren't solely engaging through digital channels. Our primary goal was to reach disengaged, unregistered voters in swing states and rural districts who show up more deeply through in-person community spaces.

What I drove.

I grew the annual publication from its first 10-page pamphlet into a 100-page annual magazine with quarterly tabloid editions. I audited comparable publications, tested 10+ paper stocks, and designed a distribution model for gyms, barbershops, bookstores, and community centers. I worked with an external team of designers, illustrators, and writers to bring each issue to life, leading art direction, editing, and end-to-end project management.

The result.

50,000 copies distributed ahead of the 2022 election cycle, fueled by the distribution model. Issue No. 3 won the 2021 Florida Print Award for Best Use of Color in Design.

07Penguin Random House · Multicultural Marketing Hiring Assignment, 2022

Such a Fun Age: A Relaunch Narrative

Built with
Reader personasReview analysisComp-title researchKPI model

The challenge.

A bestselling novel about race, class, and power, relaunching into a season of activism fatigue. Sold as "a book about race," it risked losing the readers who would love it most or feel alienated by the subject matter.

What I built.

  • Primary and secondary reader personas, with demographics, psychographics, comp titles, and brand affinities.
  • A messaging strategy built on the book's real strengths: approachability, humor, and challenge. I built it from the critical reviews too, because being challenged by a novel is as valuable as loving it.
  • Competitive positioning against The Vanishing Half and The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo: an entry point for reluctant or burnt-out readers.
  • An audience plan: author speaking engagements, influencer partners, a Multicultural Bookfluencer Affiliate Program, and TV and film co-promotion.
  • Art direction guidance that moved the original cover past pink and blue and the gender binary.

The result.

The pitch earned an offer to continue my work in multicultural marketing at Penguin Random House.

08Founder · Community learning platform and speaker series, 2020 to 2022

Allies Doing Work: Community At Scale

Built with
InstagramInstagram LiveDiscordCommunity programmingCommunity partners

The challenge.

In May 2020, people wanted to act on racial justice and didn't know where to start. Most online spaces offered outrage or performance. Few offered a place to learn together, or a way to hear from the people doing the work.

What I built.

A community centered on anti-racism work, intersectionality, and human rights advocacy, built on community before content. I set the tone early: curious, specific, and generous with people still learning.

Then I curated and hosted a two-year speaker series with leaders in human rights, nonprofit work, and organizing.

Episodes included:

  • On Colorism in the Latinx Community, with Evelynn Escobar, founder of HikeClerb
  • Blackness & Indigeneity, with Kara Roselle of the Chappaquiddick Wampanoag Tribe
  • Performative Allyship, with Sinikiwe Dhliwayo, founder of Naaya Wellness
  • Engagement at the Polls, with WorkThePolls

The result.

It grew faster than I could have planned and was profiled by Salon and Levi's Off the Cuff. The series led to paid brand partnerships: Lesse (2021), Jenni Kayne and Grayson (2022), a keynote at Naaya Wellness's The Retreat, Project Home, and Thousand Fell. Grayson paired its campaign with a $40,000 commitment to causes serving women of color (BirthFund in New York).

Global Internship Program: Scaling As A Sole Operator

Built with
TeamTailorNotionSlackUniversity Partners

The challenge.

Growing the program was the stated goal from the executive team. Scaling the program showed the real gap: managers had no shared way to run the program or connect interns' work to the organizational priorities that justified the paid investment.

What I drove.

  • Opened university relations and outreach pipelines that grew applications 620%.
  • Built a selection rubric and assessment templates for fair, consistent hiring decisions.
  • Owned the offer workflow end to end: letters, work authorization, contracts, and stipend payments.
  • Programmed the cohort experience: Ask Me Anythings with senior leaders, Entrepreneur Firesides, public speaking trainings, storytelling workshops, departmental deep dives with team leads, and 5-minute final pitches to the CEO and an executive panel.
  • Owned cohort communication through WhatsApp Communities, with daily moderation, community tending, and channel milestones that kept interns connected across offices for all 10 weeks.
  • Wrote a manager playbook and opened a shared Slack talent pool for hiring collaboration across teams.

What I changed after year one.

Interns were landing on duplicate projects with no oversight from the executive team, so I added a three-step scope review before each cohort started to ensure alignment from the top down.

The result.

The most diverse, highest-performing cohort to date, with outcomes tracked after the program ended, including retention and conversions to hires. Interns rated the program an NPS of 98, and managers rated it an NPS of 90.

10Endeavor · Global nonprofit, 42 offices

Global Onboarding: Revamped for 42 Offices

Built with
LearnDashNotionSalesforceManager TrainingBuddy Program

The challenge.

New hires in different offices started in very different worlds. Some had a clear onboarding based on their local office. Other offices lacked the support or infrastructure to ensure a consistent onboarding. Global HQ had not standardized the process across offices, and new employees often felt disengaged across the board. There was limited visibility or data to track the new employee experience.

What I drove.

I spent two months embedded in our São Paulo office, interviewed 40+ staff and managers across the region, and rebuilt onboarding as one 90-day journey that works across languages, cultures, and levels, with support from the Local People Team.

New hires start with async onboarding in LearnDash and get an automated buddy match on day 7. Their manager checks in with them at day 15, and at days 30, 60, and 90 the new hire and manager each check in individually with the People Team. Managers get training and best-practice guides, and every quarter, new hires meet as a cohort across offices and levels to build bonds and cohesion.

The result.

A clear 30-60-90 day framework for all 42 offices. Managers felt more supported in feedback, goal setting, and work planning for new hires, and early attrition decreased.

11Endeavor · Hiring exercise, March 2024

Scaling Connectivity: The Language Program

Built with
Language Matching AlgorithmCEFR levelsPre and post surveys

The challenge.

Scale connection across a global workforce of 600 people in dozens of offices, where cross-office relationships depended on who happened to meet whom. Work is async and constrained by time zones.

What I designed.

A language program people can enter small and go deeper by choice. A $1,500 Language Matching Algorithm pairs Learners and Speakers by language, proficiency, hobbies, and availability.

Every touchpoint ends in a short survey that shapes the next match, and weekly reports give the People Team a live read on what is working. It plugs into the existing Onboarding and Buddy Program instead of competing with them, to ensure seamless integration.

The result.

The design earned me an offer to join Endeavor and lead Global People Programs.
